title: Russia bombards Odesa and its port after leaving the Black Sea grain deal
body:
In the days after Moscow pulled out of the UN-brokered Black Sea grain deal, Russia bombarded the Ukrainian port city of Odesa with missiles and drones. On Tuesday, 18 July 2023, Russian missiles hit Odesa, and in the early hours of Wednesday, 19 July, a second night of attacks followed. Ukraine's air force called it one of the largest sustained aerial assaults on Odesa, Ukraine's largest port, and Odesa's regional military administration said it may have been the largest on the city since the full-scale invasion began.

Ukraine's air force said at least 30 cruise missiles and 32 attack drones were fired, mainly from the Black Sea, and that it intercepted 14 of the missiles and 23 of the drones. Officials said targets included grain terminals and other infrastructure needed to ship food. Port infrastructure was damaged, including a grain and oil terminal, tanks and loading equipment. Odesa's city government said 10 people needed medical help, including a nine-year-old boy.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia was deliberately targeting the grain deal's infrastructure in an effort to resume a de facto Black Sea blockade. Moscow denied that the attacks were related to the grain deal and called them a mass retaliatory strike on drone-manufacturing facilities. Russia said the strikes on Tuesday were retribution for the Monday attack on the bridge to Crimea. Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov warned of certain risks to shipping without appropriate security guarantees.
